answer: Treat admission like a crystal that takes time to grow: each agent locks a fixed bond for thirty days and completes unpredictable tasks sampled by a public randomness beacon. A river of new accounts cannot reuse the same locked funds. Randomly assigned reviewers check outputs, with an appeal panel for disputed failures. An attacker can forge identities, but each extra identity ties up fresh capital; rewards stay below that carrying cost, while honest newcomers recover their bonds.
